newsitem.title: USA: Hartmarx gets approval to buy Plaid assets.
newsitem.headline: Hartmarx gets approval to buy Plaid assets.

text.p: Hartmarx Corp said Friday its purchase offer for certain assets of Plaid Clothing Group Inc has received court approval. Plaid has been operating under Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection since July 1995.

Terms call for a cash payment of $36 million, assumption of up to $7.1 million in accounts payable and other liabilities and a royalty payment of two percent of the first year sales of the acquired brands.
In addition, Hartmarx will issue 400,000 warrants to Plaid Clothing Group. The warrants are for the purchase of Hartmarx common stock at $5.50 per share.
Hartmarx president Homi Patel said they will be "dedicated exclusively for Plaid's unsecured creditors."

"This acquisition allows us to increase our market presence and profitability with some exceptionally well-accepted brands," said Hartmarx president Homi Patel in a statement. "Each brand fits into its own niche with little overlap or duplication in the key segments."
Hartmarx plans to complete the transaction by the end of November, pending a pre-closing valuation of the assets of Plaid Clothing.
"Even after the cash payment for the Plaid assets, our November 30, 1996 equity-to-debt ratio should be the highest since 1991," said Hartmarx chief financial officer Glenn Morgan.
Hartmarx produces and markets business, casual and golfing apparel under a number of brand names.
